intro: New England likely loses Drake Maye for the season, Los Angeles waits on Puka Nacua until mid-December and Seattle's Jaxon Smith-Njigba owns the NFL receiving lead. Colts and Texans open Week 11 tonight, and Sunday night sends Vikings and 49ers to Mexico City. 160 stories across all 32 teams.

top.label: Biggest Story
top.headline: Patriots expect to be without Drake Maye the rest of the season
top.dek: Safety Kevin Byard told WEEI that Maye is probably done for the year, and coach Mike Vrabel does not expect him back after the bye. Adam Schefter reported the team fears a fractured ankle, though New England has not confirmed a diagnosis.

top.label: Injury Watch
top.headline: Puka Nacua stays on injured reserve until mid-December
top.dek: Nacua sprained his MCL and PCL and has turf toe, and the Rams moved him to injured reserve Nov. 12. Coach Sean McVay said the timeline has not changed. He becomes eligible to return for Week 15 against the Cowboys.

top.label: Player Spotlight
top.headline: James Cook leads the AFC with 971 rushing yards
top.dek: Cook has nine rushing touchdowns and tops every AFC back in yards. He now meets a Dolphins front missing Zach Sieler, Jordan Phillips and Zeek Biggers.

top.label: Stat of the Day
top.headline: 1,207: Jaxon Smith-Njigba's receiving yards lead the NFL
top.dek: Smith-Njigba also leads the league with 79 catches and 10 touchdowns with seven games left. No other receiver has reached 1,000 yards, and CeeDee Lamb is next at 976.

top.label: What's Next
top.headline: Vikings and 49ers meet in Mexico City on Sunday night
top.dek: Minnesota (7-2) visits San Francisco (8-1) at Estadio Banorte on Sunday, Nov. 22, at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC. Watch Kirk Cousins against Raheem Morris's disguised coverages and how both teams handle the altitude.

teams.name: Buffalo Bills
teams.headline: Bills ground game meets a thin Miami front

stories.text: Bills run game faces a gutted Dolphins front
stories.summary: Buffalo carries a five-game win streak into Sunday against a Miami defensive line that lost three tackles to injured reserve. James Cook and Josh Allen lead the AFC in rushing yards and rushing touchdowns, respectively.

stories.text: Three defensive starters sit out Wednesday
stories.summary: Cornerback Christian Benford (groin), slot corner Dee Alford (concussion protocol) and linebacker Dorian Williams (calf) did not practice. Safeties Amani Hooker and Cole Bishop were limited, and Damar Hamlin left on a scooter with a walking boot. Tight end Dalton Kincaid added a thumb issue to his ankle problem.

stories.text: James Cook leads the AFC with 971 rushing yards
stories.summary: Cook has nine rushing touchdowns on the year and tops every AFC back in yards. He now meets a Dolphins front missing Zach Sieler, Jordan Phillips and Zeek Biggers.

stories.text: 11: Josh Allen's rushing touchdowns, tops in the AFC
stories.summary: Allen scored twice on five carries against the Jets and leads the conference in rushing scores. He also threw for 196 yards in the 31-12 win.

stories.text: Dolphins visit Orchard Park Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Buffalo is 8-1 and Miami is 1-8. Watch the secondary, where Benford, Alford and Williams are all questionable, and whether the Bills start faster than they did against the Jets.

teams.name: Miami Dolphins
teams.headline: Dolphins sign Carlson, lose two more tackles

stories.text: Dolphins bring in Daniel Carlson to fix the kicker spot
stories.summary: Miami cut Zane Gonzalez after three misses in the 24-22 loss at Indianapolis and signed Carlson to the practice squad on Tuesday. Coach Jeff Hafley said he wants consistency, and Carlson is expected to be elevated for Sunday.

stories.text: Phillips and Biggers join Sieler on injured reserve
stories.summary: Jordan Phillips (torn biceps) and Zeek Biggers (knee) are done for the season. Center Aaron Brewer is still in the concussion protocol, so Andrew Meyer would start if Brewer cannot clear it.

stories.text: Kyle McCord debuts and expects another start
stories.summary: The rookie made his NFL debut and completed 17 of 32 passes for 209 yards and ran for a touchdown against the Colts. He is expected to start again in Buffalo with Malik Willis on injured reserve.

stories.text: 3: straight games under 100 rushing yards
stories.summary: Miami topped 100 yards on the ground five games in a row, then fell short in each of the last three. No Dolphins running back has scored in that stretch.

stories.text: Miami visits Buffalo Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: The Dolphins are 1-8 and face an 8-1 Bills team that has won five straight. Watch Kenneth Grant and a patched defensive tackle group against Cook and Allen.

teams.name: New England Patriots
teams.headline: Patriots on bye with Maye likely done

stories.text: Byard says Maye is probably done for the year
stories.summary: Safety Kevin Byard told WEEI that Drake Maye is likely out for the rest of the season, and coach Mike Vrabel said Monday he does not expect Maye back after the bye. Adam Schefter reported the team fears a fractured ankle, though the club has not confirmed a diagnosis.

stories.text: Maye stayed in Germany for tests after the Munich sack
stories.summary: Maye hurt his ankle on a first-quarter sack by Aidan Hutchinson in the 35-10 loss to Detroit and did not return. Vrabel called keeping him overseas a precaution and declined to give details.

stories.text: Tommy DeVito is the man after the bye
stories.summary: DeVito finished 12 of 24 for 81 yards with a touchdown and an interception in relief. Practice squad passer Behren Morton is the only other quarterback on the roster, and Vrabel does not plan to add one.

stories.text: 43: Maye's consecutive starts, and the streak is over
stories.summary: Maye had not missed a game since he took over as the starter in Week 6 of 2024. His 43 straight starts ranked third among active quarterbacks behind Josh Allen and Jared Goff.

stories.text: Bye this week, then the Chargers on Nov. 29
stories.summary: New England returns at Los Angeles on Sunday, Nov. 29 at 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS. Watch for whether the offense can climb above the 151 total yards it managed in Munich, its low for the season.

teams.name: New York Jets
teams.headline: Geno's ankle clouds Chargers trip

stories.text: Geno Smith's Sunday status stays unclear
stories.summary: Coach Aaron Glenn would not say whether Smith will start at the Chargers. Smith was a limited participant Wednesday, and rookie Cade Klubnik is next in line.

stories.text: Smith: concussion check, then an ankle injury
stories.summary: Smith left the Buffalo loss for a concussion evaluation, returned, and then hurt his ankle in the third quarter. Glenn said earlier this week Smith will start if healthy.

stories.text: Cade Klubnik steps in for Smith
stories.summary: The rookie went 11 of 20 for 137 yards with one interception after Smith went down. He is the likely starter if Smith cannot play.

stories.text: 313: Geno Smith's passing yards without a touchdown
stories.summary: Smith has no touchdown pass over his last two games, and the Jets have lost five straight. The offense has not scored a touchdown in either of those games.

stories.text: Jets at Chargers Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: New York is 2-8 and Los Angeles is 1-8 after beating Baltimore on Monday night. Watch quarterback Justin Herbert, who has 11 interceptions, against a Jets defense trying to end the skid.

teams.name: Baltimore Ravens
teams.headline: Ravens chase a win in Carolina

stories.text: Ravens try to end a five-game skid at Carolina
stories.summary: Baltimore lost 23-20 to the previously winless Chargers on Monday night and now sits last in the AFC North at 4-6. Jacoby Brissett will start again, the fourth Ravens quarterback in four weeks. The Ravens have not been to Charlotte since 2018, when the Panthers won 36-21.

stories.text: Madubuike is the lone Ravens absence at practice
stories.summary: Defensive lineman Nnamdi Madubuike sat out Wednesday with a hamstring injury. Guard Vega Ioane (knee and shoulder) and safety Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) were limited. Coach Jesse Minter said the team will see later in the week where Madubuike stands.

stories.text: Andrews posts a season-high 82 yards on eight catches
stories.summary: Tight end Mark Andrews gave Brissett a steady target against the Chargers, catching eight passes for a season-best 82 yards. Rookie running back Adam Randall was activated and could make his debut Sunday.

stories.text: 11: straight road wins for Baltimore over NFC teams
stories.summary: The Ravens have won their last 11 road games against NFC opponents, a streak they take to Carolina this weekend. Derrick Henry has 699 rushing yards and has reached 10 rushing touchdowns for the ninth straight season.

stories.text: Ravens at Panthers, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: Baltimore (4-6) visits first-place Carolina (4-5). The Panthers beat New Orleans 20-17 to snap a three-game skid, and running back Chuba Hubbard has 711 rushing yards. Watch whether Baltimore can run the ball after Henry gained 10 yards on 10 carries against the Chargers.

teams.name: Cincinnati Bengals
teams.headline: Bengals eye Monday night in Washington

stories.text: Bengals take the division lead behind a record-tying Burrow
stories.summary: Cincinnati beat Pittsburgh 38-18 to go 7-2 and move into first place in the AFC North. Joe Burrow threw four touchdown passes, which tied Peyton Manning's NFL record for five straight games with at least four combined passing and rushing scores. The Bengals gained 486 yards.

stories.text: Guard Dalton Risner questionable with knee trouble
stories.summary: Risner left the Steelers game with both knees bothering him, and Jalen Rivers played 32 snaps in his place. Safety Kyle Dugger, tackle Myles Hinton and linebacker Oren Burks are also listed as questionable for Monday. Wide receiver Andrei Iosivas remains on injured reserve.

stories.text: Chase hauls in 11 catches for 231 yards
stories.summary: Ja'Marr Chase caught 11 of 14 targets against the Steelers, a season high in catches and 76 yards above his previous best this year. Pittsburgh kept him out of the end zone. Tee Higgins added five catches for 66 yards.

stories.text: 298.9: Cincinnati's passing yards per game, tops in the NFL
stories.summary: Burrow ranks second in passing yards (2,795) and leads the league with 27 touchdown passes while completing 74 percent of his throws. Washington's pass defense ranks second worst at 244.8 yards allowed per game.

stories.text: Bengals at Commanders, Monday at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN
stories.summary: Cincinnati (7-2) visits Washington (3-5-1) at Northwest Stadium. The Commanders blitz on 35.7 percent of dropbacks, fourth highest in the league, and Burrow went 12 of 12 against Pittsburgh's blitzes. Watch the pressure from Jonathan Allen's side too.

teams.name: Cleveland Browns
teams.headline: Browns use bye to weigh Watson's future

stories.text: Watson's play has Browns thinking about his future
stories.summary: Deshaun Watson was not expected to stay in Cleveland past this season. After a 6-4 start and a booed preseason night, the team may now consider a new short-term deal. He has thrown for 300 yards in each of his last three games.

stories.text: Browns use the bye to heal; Hickman in concussion protocol
stories.summary: Safety Ronnie Hickman is listed as questionable for Week 12 with a concussion. Guard Teven Jenkins and running back Raheim Sanders are on injured reserve and expected back for the Raiders game. Rookie receiver Denzel Boston played through a toe injury Sunday.

stories.text: Corley moves up to the No. 4 receiver spot
stories.summary: Malachi Corley had his highest offensive snap share of the season against Houston and converted key third downs, including a sliding catch that set up a go-ahead field goal. He has passed Isaiah Bond, who played one offensive snap.

stories.text: 312: Watson's passing yards in the comeback over Houston
stories.summary: Watson also ran seven times for 50 yards and a touchdown as Cleveland erased a 17-0 deficit to win 27-24. The Browns have been outscored badly in first quarters this season, and coach Todd Monken says the slow starts need fixing.

stories.text: Bye now, then Raiders on Sunday Night Football Nov. 29
stories.summary: Cleveland (6-4) is off in Week 11 and holds the seventh seed in the AFC. The Week 12 game against Las Vegas was flexed to Sunday Night Football and kicks off at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC.

teams.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
teams.headline: Steelers lose McCormick, get receivers back

stories.text: Steelers place guard McCormick on IR, Anderson steps in
stories.summary: Mason McCormick dislocated his ankle against the Bengals and went on injured reserve Wednesday. He needs no surgery, but he will miss at least four games, with Dec. 20 at Baltimore the earliest return. Spencer Anderson takes over at left guard.

stories.text: Herbig sits out as three IR players return to practice
stories.summary: Linebacker Nick Herbig (hip and ribs) did not practice Wednesday, and Patrick Queen (hand) and DeShon Elliott (knee) were limited. Receivers Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson and guard Gennings Dunker returned to practice from injured reserve. Coach Mike McCarthy said it is unclear whether any of them play Sunday.

stories.text: Roman Wilson is back at practice with 14 catches already
stories.summary: Wilson has 14 catches for 188 yards and two touchdowns this season and returned to practice from injured reserve this week. Michael Pittman Jr. also returned and has seven catches for 89 yards in three games. Either could be activated within a 21-day window.

stories.text: 39: straight starts for McCormick end
stories.summary: McCormick had started 39 consecutive games since 2024 and moved from right guard to left guard this year. His injury came in a 38-18 loss that left Pittsburgh a game behind Cincinnati.

stories.text: Steelers at Eagles, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Pittsburgh (6-3) visits 2-7 Philadelphia at Lincoln Financial Field after the NFL flexed the game from 4:25 p.m. to 1 p.m. The Steelers allowed 484 net yards to Cincinnati, and Cam Heyward says the fixes start in practice.

teams.name: Houston Texans
teams.headline: Texans face Colts with a 20% playoff chance

stories.text: Texans host Colts on Thursday night with their season on the line
stories.summary: Houston is 3-6 after blowing a 17-point lead in Cleveland. Next Gen Stats puts its playoff odds at 20%, dropping to 7% with a loss. The Texans sit four games behind Jacksonville and 2.5 games behind Cleveland for the last wild-card spot.

stories.text: Hunter, Harrison and Marks out; Montgomery cleared
stories.summary: Edge Danielle Hunter and receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. are out with hamstring injuries. Running back Woody Marks is out with a concussion and tight end Brevin Jordan will not play. David Montgomery carries no designation after missing four games with a groin injury. Cornerback Jaylin Smith, linebacker Jake Hummel and guard Wyatt Teller are questionable.

stories.text: Nico Collins piles up 16 targets in Cleveland
stories.summary: Collins caught 9 passes for 94 yards and a touchdown on 16 targets against the Browns. He has drawn 55 targets from C.J. Stroud over seven games. With Harrison out again, he is the clear first read.

stories.text: 4: Houston has lost four games it led in the fourth quarter, most in the NFL
stories.summary: The Texans have also blown a lead inside the final two minutes four times. Only one of the 14 teams since 1982 with four or more such losses in a season reached the playoffs, the 2022 Ravens. Houston's offense went three-and-out on six of its last eight drives against Cleveland.

stories.text: Colts tonight, then Ravens at home Nov. 29
stories.summary: Houston hosts Indianapolis tonight at 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video. The Colts beat the Texans 19-17 in Week 3. Watch Houston's ground game, which ranks 29th in rushing yards per game, against a Colts offense that ran for a season-high 172 yards last week.

teams.name: Indianapolis Colts
teams.headline: Colts down five starters for Thursday night

stories.text: Colts try to sweep Houston with a gutted roster
stories.summary: Indianapolis is 3-7 and has lost 14 of its last 17 games. Its playoff odds sit under 5%. Alec Pierce is on injured reserve, and Keenan Allen and Josh Downs were traded before the deadline. Daniel Jones leads a passing game with a sub-60% completion rate and 12 interceptions.

stories.text: Colts rule out five, Gardner questionable
stories.summary: Cornerback Charvarius Ward (knee), tackles Bernhard Raimann (concussion) and Jalen Travis (knee), tight end Will Mallory (hamstring) and defensive tackle Jerry Tillery (calf) are out. Sauce Gardner is questionable with a calf injury after leaving Sunday's game. Linebacker Jaylon Carlies went to injured reserve Tuesday.

stories.text: Jonathan Taylor carries the offense on a thin snap count
stories.summary: Taylor ran 16 times for 83 yards against Miami after 13 carries for 46 the week before. He has played under 70% of snaps in four straight games. He has at least 50 rushing yards in seven of 10 games.

stories.text: 17: Taylor's career-long streak without a 100-yard game
stories.summary: Taylor has not topped 100 rushing yards in 17 straight games. The Colts have not won when he is held under 65 yards since November 2024. Indianapolis ran for a season-high 172 yards against Miami.

stories.text: At Houston tonight, then Giants at home Nov. 29
stories.summary: The Colts kick off at 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video. They face a Houston defense ranked 11th against the run, missing leading tackler Azeez Al-Shaair. Will Anderson Jr., the league sack leader, meets an Indianapolis tackle group missing Raimann and Travis.

teams.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
teams.headline: Jaguars start backup center at the Giants

stories.text: Jaguars take a three-game win streak to MetLife
stories.summary: Jacksonville is 7-2 and visits the 5-3-1 Giants, leaders of the NFC East. Liam Coen expects the game to be decided at the line of scrimmage. The Giants rank fifth in the NFL in yards allowed and give J.J. McCarthy, 2-1 as a starter, a run-first offense under John Harbaugh.

stories.text: Hainsey out with knee sprain, 10 Jaguars limited
stories.summary: Center Robert Hainsey sprained his knee against Tennessee and is week-to-week. He will miss Sunday. Ten players were limited Wednesday, among them Travon Walker (rib), Jakobi Meyers (ankle), Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) and Danny Striggow (concussion). BJ Green (forearm) was a full participant.

stories.text: Jonah Monheim steps in at center
stories.summary: The second-year seventh-round pick will make his first start of 2026. He played 33 snaps in Week 10 after Hainsey got hurt. Coen said Monheim has taken many first-team reps and works well with Trevor Lawrence.

stories.text: 305.7: Yards per game the Giants allow, fifth in the NFL
stories.summary: New York also ranks third against the pass at 184.1 yards per game. Jacksonville's line will see varied pressure looks, and Coen wants it blitz-ready. The Giants' defensive front includes Abdul Carter, Arvell Reese and Kayvon Thibodeaux.

stories.text: At the Giants Sunday, then Titans at home Nov. 29
stories.summary: Kickoff is 4:25 p.m. ET Sunday at MetLife Stadium on CBS. Giants tight end Isaiah Likely has 55 catches for 575 yards and seven touchdowns. New Jaguars tackle Jordan Davis, acquired in a trade, faces a division rival of his old Eagles team.

teams.name: Tennessee Titans
teams.headline: Robinson lands on IR as Titans visit Dallas

stories.text: Titans put Wan'Dale Robinson on injured reserve
stories.summary: Robinson hurt his ankle late in the 40-23 loss to Jacksonville and will miss at least four games. He led Tennessee with 38 catches, 272 yards and three touchdowns. Xavier Restrepo moved up from the practice squad.

stories.text: Spears and Adams sit out Wednesday, Tate returns
stories.summary: Running back Tyjae Spears (knee) and safety Tony Adams (concussion) did not practice. Receiver Carnell Tate was limited with a shoulder injury after missing two games. Guard Fernando Carmona, defensive lineman John Franklin-Myers and linebacker Anthony Hill Jr. were also limited.

stories.text: Carnell Tate back at practice with 413 yards
stories.summary: The rookie first-round pick practiced Wednesday after missing two games. He has 34 catches for 413 yards and one touchdown. With Robinson on injured reserve, Tate is now Cam Ward's top target.

stories.text: 38: Catches by Robinson, a team high before his injury
stories.summary: Robinson signed a four-year, $70 million deal in March to reunite with coordinator Brian Daboll. He had seasons of 90-plus catches under Daboll with the Giants. Tate trails him in catches but leads Tennessee in yards.

stories.text: At Dallas Sunday, then at Jacksonville Nov. 29
stories.summary: Tennessee plays the Cowboys at 1 p.m. ET Sunday on Fox. The Titans will wear a never-before-used light blue uniform combination. After Dallas they travel to Jacksonville for a rematch of last Sunday's loss.

teams.name: Denver Broncos
teams.headline: Payton's playcalling has the Broncos scoring again

stories.text: Payton took over the play sheet and the Broncos offense woke up
stories.summary: Sean Payton took playcalling back from Davis Webb after a 2-2 start, and Denver has gone 5-0 since. The offense climbed from 16.8 points per game to 24.8. Payton still wants the points to arrive before the fourth quarter, so the Broncos stop living in one-score games.

stories.text: Waddle and Moss practice fully, Hufanga is back too
stories.summary: Every active Bronco practiced Wednesday. Jaylen Waddle, Riley Moss and Adam Prentice went full through concussion protocol, and Talanoa Hufanga had his first full practice since Week 5. Brandon Jones and Kris Abrams-Draine returned on a limited basis, and tight end Caleb Lohner opened his 21-day window off injured reserve.

stories.text: Pat Bryant makes his case after four weeks on injured reserve
stories.summary: The second-year receiver returned from an ankle injury in Week 9 and caught four passes for 56 yards and a 26-yard touchdown from Bo Nix. Waddle's early exit with a concussion gave him extra snaps. Payton praised his hands in traffic and his run after the catch.

stories.text: 5 of 11: Nix's touchdown passes that came in the fourth quarter
stories.summary: Bo Nix has thrown nearly half of his touchdown passes in the final period. He has also topped 220 passing yards in each of his last three games, after doing it twice in the first six. Payton says he does not have a clean answer for the slow starts.

stories.text: Raiders visit Empower Field on Sunday at 4:25 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Denver hosts Las Vegas after the bye with a five-game winning streak. The Raiders allow 28.9 points per game, tied for last in the league, so the offense has a chance to score early. Las Vegas leads the all-time series, but Denver won the last meeting 24-17.

teams.name: Kansas City Chiefs
teams.headline: Chiefs go for 5-0 at home against shaky Arizona

stories.text: Chiefs look for a fifth home win against a reeling Cardinals team
stories.summary: Kansas City hosts Arizona at 7-2 and trails Denver only on tiebreakers. The Cardinals are 3-7, start rookie Carson Beck again after Gardner Minshew's season-ending elbow injury, and have been outscored 51-9 over two games. Andy Reid said the Chiefs are still annoyed about missing the playoffs last year.

stories.text: Smith, Moore and Walker sit out Wednesday's practice
stories.summary: Right guard Trey Smith (concussion), right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) and running back Kenneth Walker III (groin) did not practice. Nick Bolton (shin) and Omarr Norman-Lott (knee) were limited. Rookie lineman Peter Woods and running back Jaydn Ott returned to full work, and final game designations come Friday.

stories.text: Mahomes plays through an elbow issue and throws for 348
stories.summary: Patrick Mahomes threw for 348 yards and five touchdowns against Atlanta, his first five-touchdown game since 2022. He did it while carrying an elbow injury from the week before. Reid said Mahomes is staying in the pocket when he should and moving when he needs to.

stories.text: 17.3: points per game the Chiefs defense allows, third in the NFL
stories.summary: Kansas City also ranks eighth in total defense at 314.8 yards per game. The offense has scored 30 or more points five times this season. That mix has made the Chiefs a serious threat in the AFC.

stories.text: Cardinals visit Arrowhead on Sunday at 1 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Arizona has not gotten a touchdown pass from its starting quarterback in three straight games. Watch the Chiefs offensive line without Smith and Moore if they do not clear. A short week follows, with a Thanksgiving night game at Buffalo.

teams.name: Las Vegas Raiders
teams.headline: Raiders worry about Mendoza taking hits

stories.text: Former lineman flags Mendoza's pocket awareness before Denver
stories.summary: Lincoln Kennedy, a former Raiders tackle, said rookie Fernando Mendoza misses blitzers and has to stop absorbing so many hits. Seattle sacked Mendoza six times in a 21-13 loss, and Las Vegas has lost six of its last seven. Maxx Crosby praised the rookie's leadership.

stories.text: Bowers and Hemingway miss Wednesday's practice with ankle injuries
stories.summary: Tight end Brock Bowers did not practice after leaving the Seattle game in the second quarter following 11 snaps. Defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway also sat out with an ankle injury. Folorunso Fatukasi (toe) and kicker Matt Gay (hip) were limited, and Thomas Booker returned to full practice.

stories.text: Bowers leads the Raiders in every receiving category, now with an ankle
stories.summary: Brock Bowers has 50 catches for 676 yards and six touchdowns, all team highs. His absence would leave Mendoza without his top target against a Broncos pass rush that sits in the top 10 in sacks. Las Vegas lists him as day to day.

stories.text: 28.9: points per game the Raiders allow, tied for last in the NFL
stories.summary: The defense ranks 31st in scoring while the offense scores 25.1 per game, 10th in the league. Denver's offense ranks 30th in total yards, so this game tests which weakness gives way.

stories.text: Raiders visit Denver on Sunday at 4:25 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Las Vegas leads the all-time series 72-57-2 but lost 24-17 to Denver last December. Maxx Crosby needs half a sack to reach 75 career sacks. Mendoza faces a Broncos defense that allows 20.7 points per game.

teams.name: Los Angeles Chargers
teams.headline: Chargers try to stack a second win against the Jets

stories.text: Chargers chase back-to-back wins against a Jets team in a skid
stories.summary: Los Angeles ended an eight-game losing streak with a 23-20 win at Baltimore on Monday night. The Jets are 2-8 and have lost five straight, and they have not beaten the Chargers in five meetings. Geno Smith is limited with an ankle injury but expects to play.

stories.text: Henley, Kolar, Shelley and Thompson out, McConkey limited
stories.summary: Linebacker Daiyan Henley (knee), tight end Charlie Kolar (concussion), defensive back Rodney Shelley (ankle) and receiver Brenen Thompson (hamstring) are out. Receiver Ladd McConkey (back) was limited Wednesday after missing the past two games.

stories.text: Herbert adds 51 rushing yards and a 22-yard touchdown run
stories.summary: Justin Herbert threw no touchdown passes in Baltimore but made plays with his legs, scrambling for a 22-yard score. He also threw no interceptions, after at least one in every earlier game. Tarheeb Still stripped Zay Flowers late to help seal the win.

stories.text: 16.0: points per game, last in the NFL
stories.summary: The Chargers still run the ball well, ranking 11th at 119.6 yards per game, and ran for a season-high 160 against Baltimore. The defense gives up 343.7 yards per game, up from 285.2 last season.

stories.text: Jets visit SoFi Stadium on Sunday at 4:05 PM ET on Fox
stories.summary: It is the first Jets-Chargers game at SoFi since 2020. The Jets rank 30th against the run, allowing 135.3 yards per game, which fits a Chargers offense built around Omarion Hampton. New York may start Geno Smith or rookie Cade Klubnik.

teams.name: Dallas Cowboys
teams.headline: Pettine gets defensive calls after 584-yard night

stories.text: Cowboys hand defensive play-calling to Mike Pettine
stories.summary: Dallas changed course on defense Wednesday, three days after the 49ers piled up 584 yards in a 46-40 win. Coach Brian Schottenheimer is moving the play-calling to Mike Pettine, and coordinator Christian Parker's future is unclear. Jerry Jones said Tuesday the team is discussing it and that he always expected adjustments.

stories.text: Ferguson, Bland and Booker all miss Wednesday practice
stories.summary: Tight end Jake Ferguson has a sprained PCL and MCL in his left knee and is not expected to face Tennessee. Cornerback DaRon Bland (high ankle sprain) and guard Tyler Booker (high ankle sprain) also sat out, and T.J. Bass steps in for Booker at right guard. Safety P.J. Locke III (concussion), linebacker Donovan Ezeiruaku and receiver Jonathan Mingo (both ankle) are unsettled until Friday.

stories.text: Javonte Williams searches for steady yards on the ground
stories.summary: Williams averaged 2.3 yards per carry against Arizona in Week 8, 5.0 against Indianapolis in Week 9 and 3.9 against San Francisco last Sunday. Dallas has 1,028 rushing yards, 21st in the league. Tennessee's defense gives him a chance to settle the number.

stories.text: 48.8%: the third-down rate Cowboys opponents convert
stories.summary: That is the worst mark in the NFL. San Francisco went 6 for 11 on third down last Sunday, and Dallas also ranks 32nd in rushing yards allowed. Those two numbers explain much of the 584 yards.

stories.text: Titans visit AT&T Stadium Sunday at 1:00 PM ET on FOX
stories.summary: Tennessee is 1-8 and brings former Cowboy Tony Pollard, who has 628 rushing yards. Dallas has a run defense to fix against him. The Cowboys host Philadelphia on Thanksgiving Day after this game.

teams.name: New York Giants
teams.headline: Giants prep for 7-2 Jaguars with the division lead

stories.text: Giants keep the NFC East lead and turn to Jacksonville
stories.summary: At 5-3-1, the Giants still lead the division after Thursday's 24-21 loss in Washington. John Harbaugh called the Jaguars good in every phase and said the loss does not change the team's goals. Jacksonville comes to MetLife at 7-2 and has Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates making their debuts for the team.

stories.text: Nic Jones sits out with a knee injury, Skattebo practices fully
stories.summary: Cornerback Nic Jones did not practice Wednesday, and Patricia Traina notes he is a candidate for injured reserve. Linebacker Malik Harrison (groin) and safety Jason Pinnock (hip) were limited. Cam Skattebo (hamstring) and Deonte Banks (shoulder) went full.

stories.text: Arvell Reese earns NFC Defensive Player of the Week
stories.summary: The rookie linebacker had 12 tackles, three sacks and a forced fumble in the 19-11 win over Philadelphia. At 21 years and 70 days, he is the youngest player in NFL history with three sacks in a game. He also won Pepsi Rookie of the Week for the second time.

stories.text: 4: straight games of 30 or more points for Jacksonville
stories.summary: The Jaguars beat Tennessee 40-23 last week, and Trevor Lawrence threw for 352 yards and three touchdowns. New York's defense has to slow that streak at MetLife.

stories.text: Jaguars visit MetLife Sunday at 4:25 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: The game was flexed into the late CBS window. Jacksonville leads the AFC South at 7-2. The series is tied 4-4, and the Giants won the last meeting 23-17 in 2022.

teams.name: Philadelphia Eagles
teams.headline: Eagles stick with Milton at quarterback

stories.text: Sirianni names Joe Milton the starter against Pittsburgh
stories.summary: Nick Sirianni said Wednesday that Milton will start again and Sean Mannion will keep calling plays. Tanner McKee stays the backup, with rookie Cole Payton third on the depth chart. The Eagles have lost seven straight and come out of the bye at 2-7.

stories.text: DeVonta Smith returns to practice, Hurts still out
stories.summary: Smith was back on the field Wednesday after missing time. Jalen Hurts remains out indefinitely with a blood clot, and Milton took over after the Eagles signed him on Oct. 16.

stories.text: Joe Milton gets a second start after a rough first
stories.summary: Milton went 18 of 34 for 169 yards with no touchdowns in the 19-11 loss to the Giants, and he lost a fumble. He did run nine times for 64 yards and scored a two-point conversion. He is 26 and was a sixth-round pick of the Patriots in 2024.

stories.text: 7: sacks Joe Milton took against the Giants
stories.summary: Milton went down seven times in his first Eagles start. Pittsburgh now tests an offensive line that has to protect him better.

stories.text: Steelers visit the Linc Sunday at 1:00 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Pittsburgh is 6-3 but is coming off a 38-18 loss to Cincinnati. The Eagles then play at Dallas on Thanksgiving Day. CBS Philadelphia says Philadelphia is in position for a top-five pick with eight games left.

teams.name: Washington Commanders
teams.headline: Commanders face Burrow with a thin secondary

stories.text: Commanders ride Thursday's win into a Monday night test
stories.summary: Washington beat the Giants 24-21 to keep its playoff hopes alive and now hosts a 7-2 Cincinnati team that has won five straight. Joe Burrow threw for 409 yards and four touchdowns against Pittsburgh. The Commanders last scored more than 30 points in Week 3.

stories.text: Croskey-Merritt cleared to practice, could play Monday
stories.summary: Running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) was designated to return from injured reserve and has a 21-day window. If he is activated, he likely leads the backfield and Rachaad White moves to a pass-catching role. Terry McLaurin is out for the year with a torn patellar tendon.

stories.text: Ben Sinnott has a career game filling in for Okonkwo
stories.summary: Sinnott caught four passes for 42 yards and a touchdown against the Giants, the best game of his career. He stepped in after starting tight end Chig Okonkwo left with a back injury. Sinnott was a second-round pick in 2024.

stories.text: 244.8: passing yards per game Washington allows
stories.summary: That is the second-most in the NFL, according to the Bengals' scouting report, and Burrow averages 310.6 passing yards per game. Washington also blitzes at the third-highest rate in the league, 42.1 percent.

stories.text: Bengals visit Monday night, 8:15 PM ET on ESPN
stories.summary: Cincinnati is 7-2 and has scored 30 or more points in all five games of its win streak. Washington has to find a way to slow Ja'Marr Chase, who had 231 yards on 11 catches last week. The Commanders play at Arizona next.

teams.name: Chicago Bears
teams.headline: Bears want fumbles and flags fixed after bye

stories.text: Johnson wants ball security and penalties fixed before Saints
stories.summary: Ben Johnson put two problems on the table as the 7-2 Bears came off their bye. Chicago has fumbled 12 times and lost eight, twice as many lost fumbles as all of last season. The offense has also drawn 23 pre-snap penalties, a total only four teams exceed.

stories.text: Gordon out, Simmons limited, Burden cleared
stories.summary: Cornerback Kyler Gordon (shoulder) would not have practiced Wednesday, and defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons (knee) would have been limited, according to the estimated report the Bears released after their bye. Receiver Luther Burden is out of concussion protocol with no designation. Running back Kyle Monangai and cornerback Malik Muhammad carry no designation.

stories.text: Williams ranks second in completion rate from the pocket
stories.summary: Caleb Williams completes 74.2 percent of his passes from the pocket, second in the NFL behind Joe Burrow among quarterbacks with 100 attempts. He averages 8.4 yards per attempt there, also second. The four-interception game against Tampa Bay is the one blemish, and Johnson called it an aberration.

stories.text: -4: Bears' turnover margin ranks 29th in the league
stories.summary: Johnson himself cited the minus-four margin when he talked about ball security. Chicago still has 13 takeaways, tied for 10th, and leads the league in time of possession at 34:31 per game. New Orleans is the only team with more lost fumbles than the Bears.

stories.text: Saints visit Soldier Field Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Chicago (7-2) hosts New Orleans (3-6) in Week 11. Watch the run game: the Saints allow 129.8 rushing yards per game, sixth most, and the Bears averaged nearly 100 more rushing yards per game with Monangai this season. Saints edge rushers Chase Young and Carl Granderson have 8 sacks each.

teams.name: Detroit Lions
teams.headline: Lions regroup without Hutchinson, Joseph returns

stories.text: Lions vow to pick up the slack without Hutchinson
stories.summary: Detroit (7-2, five straight wins) turns to the Buccaneers after losing Aidan Hutchinson to a torn right ACL in Munich. Coach Dan Campbell said no one player replaces him and the group will "pick up the slack." The Lions also remain without linebacker Jack Campbell, who suffered a severe neck injury against Minnesota.

stories.text: Kerby Joseph set for season debut on a pitch count
stories.summary: Safety Kerby Joseph came off the PUP list and the Lions plan to play him Sunday, Campbell said, though on a pitch count. Joseph missed the last 11 games of 2025 with a chronic knee injury. The Lions placed Hutchinson on injured reserve to open the roster spot.

stories.text: Gibbs leads the league with 1,000 rushing yards
stories.summary: Jahmyr Gibbs was named NFC Offensive Player of the Week after 153 rushing yards, two rushing touchdowns and 99 receiving yards in Munich. He leads all running backs in rushing yards (1,000), scrimmage yards (1,384) and total touchdowns (13). He has topped 100 rushing yards in four of his last five games.

stories.text: 79.1: rushing yards per game the Bucs allow, best in the NFL
stories.summary: Tampa Bay's run defense has held each of its last eight opponents under 100 rushing yards, the longest such streak in the league this season. Gibbs, the NFL's leading rusher, faces the toughest ground test of his year. The Bucs also run the ball best in the league at 163.9 yards per game.

stories.text: Buccaneers visit Ford Field Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Detroit (7-2) is 5-0 at home and hosts Tampa Bay (3-6), whose quarterback Baker Mayfield is questionable with a foot injury. Rookie Jalon Daniels starts if Mayfield sits, and Todd Bowles said the Bucs would decide Friday. Watch how Detroit's defense, allowing 14.4 points per game during the win streak, handles life without Hutchinson.

teams.name: Green Bay Packers
teams.headline: Packers aim for Parsons debut after the bye

stories.text: LaFleur plans for Parsons to return against the Rams
stories.summary: Matt LaFleur said the plan is to have Micah Parsons back for the Thanksgiving Eve game at the Rams, though Parsons still has a couple more hurdles to clear. He tore his left ACL and meniscus last December and joined 11-on-11 drills last week. The bye is short, with players off Tuesday through Thursday.

stories.text: Zeitler, Rhyan and Parsons headline the bye-week list
stories.summary: Guard Kevin Zeitler hurt his triceps in practice before the Vikings game, and Travis Glover started in his place. Zeitler could make his first Packers start against the Rams. Guard Sean Rhyan's ankle injury, four games old, still keeps him out, and Brandon Cisse is not expected to miss time.

stories.text: McKinney leads the NFL with six interceptions
stories.summary: Safety Xavier McKinney picked off Kirk Cousins before halftime against Minnesota for his sixth interception of the season, the most in the league. The Packers needed it: they trailed 17-0 after their first four possessions. Lukas Van Ness leads the team with six sacks.

stories.text: 220: total yards for Green Bay against Minnesota
stories.summary: The Packers went 3-of-10 on third down, failed on their only red-zone trip and committed four turnovers in the 30-10 loss. Jordan Love was sacked eight times and hit 12 times. Green Bay is the first team to allow eight sacks and commit four turnovers in one game since 2023.

stories.text: Bye now, then at the Rams Wednesday at 8 p.m. ET on Netflix
stories.summary: Green Bay (6-4) sits last in the NFC North and tied with Seattle and the Rams for the seventh seed. The Packers visit Los Angeles on Wednesday, Nov. 25, then play at New Orleans on Dec. 6 and host Buffalo on Dec. 13. Watch whether Parsons and Zeitler both return.

teams.name: Minnesota Vikings
teams.headline: Vikings head to Mexico City for a 49ers test

stories.text: Vikings call 8-1 49ers a measuring-stick game
stories.summary: Minnesota (7-2) flies to Mexico City to face the top seed in the NFC. Kevin O'Connell called San Francisco a significant challenge and said the 49ers do everything well in all three phases. Kirk Cousins has already seen defensive coordinator Raheem Morris's disguised coverages this month with the Raiders.

stories.text: Addison avoids IR but will miss the 49ers
stories.summary: Receiver Jordan Addison had thumb surgery and did not practice Wednesday. O'Connell said the surgery went well enough that he is not a short-term injured reserve candidate, though Addison will not play Sunday. Tight end T.J. Hockenson (wrist) was limited, and Jauan Jennings (calf) and linebacker Blake Cashman (concussion) were full participants.

stories.text: Turner's eighth sack ties his career high in one season
stories.summary: Dallas Turner beat left tackle Jordan Morgan with a bull rush for his eighth sack, matching his 2025 total. Next Gen Stats credited him with four pressures against Morgan on 13 snaps. His 19 career sacks trail only Danielle Hunter and Alan Page among Vikings aged 23 or younger.

stories.text: 35: minutes the Vikings held the ball at Lambeau Field
stories.summary: Cousins went 21-of-31 for 207 yards and two touchdowns in the 30-10 win. Minnesota led 17-0 at halftime and sacked Jordan Love eight times, the most by a Vikings team at Lambeau. The win ended a two-game losing streak and put Minnesota in a three-way tie for first.

stories.text: At 49ers in Mexico City Sunday at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC
stories.summary: The Vikings visit San Francisco (8-1) at Estadio Banorte, their only international game of the year. Watch Cousins against Morris's disguised looks, ball security on both sides, and how Minnesota handles the altitude. Hockenson and Cashman are trending toward playing.

teams.name: Atlanta Falcons
teams.headline: Stefanski turns the bye into a self-scout

stories.text: Stefanski calls the bye a chance to learn hard lessons
stories.summary: Atlanta enters its bye 3-7 after a 35-13 home loss to Kansas City, its third straight defeat. Kevin Stefanski took the blame and said the staff will pick apart everything from practice plans to the game-plan process. Six of the team's nine penalties against the Chiefs came from offensive linemen.

stories.text: Deablo gets time to heal a broken forearm
stories.summary: Linebacker Divine Deablo sat out the Kansas City game. He has played just one game this season with a cast on his fractured right forearm, and the bye gives him extra recovery time. Receiver Drake London was cleared after a concussion check and finished the game.

stories.text: Drake London posts 109 yards in a lost cause
stories.summary: London caught six passes for 109 yards against the Chiefs. It was his 14th career game with 100 or more receiving yards, the fifth most in franchise history. Atlanta's offense gave him little help early, going without a first down on its first four drives.

stories.text: 13: interceptions thrown by Falcons quarterbacks, most in the NFL
stories.summary: Four different Atlanta quarterbacks have combined for a league-high 13 picks this season. The team's minus-10 turnover margin is tied for second worst in the league. Michael Penix Jr. has six interceptions and one touchdown pass over the last three games.

stories.text: Bye now, then a trip to 7-2 Minnesota
stories.summary: Atlanta has no game in Week 11. The Falcons visit the Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 29 at 1 p.m. ET on Fox. Minnesota is 7-2, so the first game back is a tough test of whether the bye changed anything.

teams.name: Carolina Panthers
teams.headline: First place in the South, Ravens up next

stories.text: Panthers sit atop the NFC South at 4-5
stories.summary: Carolina beat New Orleans 20-17 on Ryan Fitzgerald's 54-yard field goal as time expired and holds first place in a weak division. The Panthers were flagged 17 times for 152 yards and still won. Baltimore visits Charlotte on Sunday.

stories.text: Okereke still out, Jackson and Brooks practice in full
stories.summary: Linebacker Bobby Okereke (foot) has not practiced and looks unlikely for Sunday. Tight ends Darren Waller and Tommy Tremble and linebacker Isaiah Simmons (all knee) also sat out Wednesday. Safety Mike Jackson and running back Jonathon Brooks both practiced fully, and Jackson expects to play.

stories.text: Chuba Hubbard piles up 172 yards from scrimmage
stories.summary: Hubbard ran for 92 yards and two touchdowns against the Saints. He added five catches for 80 yards. His second short score put Carolina up 17-14 with 1:49 left.

stories.text: 0: games Bryce Young has missed despite knee, ankle and foot issues
stories.summary: Young has dealt with a knee problem, an ankle problem and now a sore foot, and has not missed a game this season. He practiced fully Wednesday, and coach Dave Canales saw no restrictions. Young went 17 of 30 for 200 yards with no turnovers against the Saints.

stories.text: Ravens visit Charlotte without Lamar Jackson
stories.summary: Baltimore (4-6, five straight losses) plays at Carolina on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 1 p.m. ET on Fox. Lamar Jackson and backup Tyler Huntley are on injured reserve, and the Ravens brought in Jacoby Brissett. Carolina then plays at Tampa Bay on Nov. 30.

teams.name: New Orleans Saints
teams.headline: Moore wants fewer self-inflicted wounds

stories.text: Moore says the Saints keep beating themselves
stories.summary: After the 20-17 loss to Carolina, Kellen Moore called the result a disappointment and said he needs to call a more aggressive game. New Orleans is 1-4 at home and had only 107 yards in the first half. A pass interference call on Kool-Aid McKinstry set up Carolina's winning kick.

stories.text: Six Saints sit out Wednesday, led by Werner and McCoy
stories.summary: Linebacker Pete Werner (hamstring), center Erik McCoy (biceps), tackles Taliese Fuaga and Asim Richards (both knee) and cornerback Martin Emerson Jr. (concussion) did not practice. Receiver Jordyn Tyson (chest) was limited. Alvin Kamara sat for rest.

stories.text: Alvin Kamara scores twice on three touches
stories.summary: Kamara got his first touch in the third quarter and ran in from 3 yards. He added a 4-yard touchdown catch in the fourth quarter. He finished with 8 yards on three touches and both Saints touchdowns.

stories.text: 11: sacks for Chase Young, with Granderson at 10
stories.summary: Young has 11 sacks and 41 pressures, and Carl Granderson has 10 sacks. The pass rush is the team's strength. New Orleans ranks 31st in both rush EPA and rush success rate allowed on defense.

stories.text: Saints go to Chicago to face the 7-2 Bears
stories.summary: New Orleans plays at Chicago on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 1 p.m. ET on Fox. Chris Olave has 59 catches for 764 yards, and the Bears have struggled against deep throws. The Saints rank last in rush success rate on offense.

teams.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
teams.headline: Bucs sit one game back with Mayfield in doubt

stories.text: Bucs are 3-6 but one game out of first
stories.summary: Tampa Bay is 2-0 in the division and trails Carolina by one game after the bye. The team rushes better than anyone in the league and passes worse than anyone. The Bucs lost 27-24 at Chicago before the bye despite forcing five turnovers.

stories.text: Mayfield and Winfield sit out Wednesday
stories.summary: Quarterback Baker Mayfield (foot, right thumb) and safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (ankle) did not practice. Edge rusher Yaya Diaby (knee) was limited. The team will decide on Mayfield on Friday, and rookie Jalon Daniels took the first-team reps.

stories.text: Bucky Irving has 825 rushing yards and seven scores
stories.summary: Irving has played every game and carries the league's best rushing attack. Kenny Gainwell has added 305 rushing yards. With the passing game ranked last, Irving's workload decides how far this offense goes.

stories.text: 324: rushing yards in a franchise-record 16-0 win over Atlanta
stories.summary: Tampa Bay set a team record for rushing yards in its shutout of the Falcons. The defense ranks fourth in yards allowed at 292.9 per game. Mayfield has three touchdown passes against seven turnovers this season.

stories.text: Bucs visit the 7-2 Lions on Sunday
stories.summary: Tampa Bay plays at Detroit on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 1 p.m. ET. Then Carolina visits Tampa on Monday, Nov. 30 on ESPN. If Mayfield can't go, Daniels would start.

teams.name: Arizona Cardinals
teams.headline: Beck and the Cardinals face Kansas City next

stories.text: Cardinals stick with rookie Carson Beck for a trip to Arrowhead
stories.summary: Carson Beck made his first NFL start in the 34-6 loss to the Rams. He went 11 of 18 for 108 yards with two interceptions and took five sacks. Coach Mike LaFleur still came away encouraged by his command of the huddle and cadence. Beck now gets a second start against the 7-2 Chiefs.

stories.text: Five Cardinals sit out Wednesday, led by Baker and Sweat
stories.summary: Safety Budda Baker, guard Isaac Seumalo, linebacker Mack Wilson and edge rusher Josh Sweat did not practice Wednesday, mostly for rest. Defensive lineman Walter Nolen missed with an illness. Center Hjalte Froholdt (concussion), guard Jon Gaines (ankle) and left tackle Jayden Williams (knee) were limited.

stories.text: Trey McBride keeps the Cardinals offense moving
stories.summary: McBride has 78 catches for 635 yards and five touchdowns on 99 targets. That is about 27.5 percent of Arizona's 360 targets. He caught all five passes thrown his way against the Rams and ranks second among NFL tight ends in receiving yards, behind Brock Bowers.

stories.text: 649: Penalty yards Arizona has given away in 10 games
stories.summary: The Cardinals have been flagged 72 times for 649 yards, more than 64 yards a game. That total is about two-thirds of their 95.8 rushing yards per game. They have also allowed 28 sacks and score touchdowns on 42.9 percent of red-zone trips.

stories.text: Cardinals visit the Chiefs Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Arizona (3-7) plays at Arrowhead Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 22, with CBS carrying the game. The Cardinals have not scored a touchdown since their 33-30 win in Dallas to open the month. Watch whether Beck can keep Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs' offense off the field.

teams.name: Los Angeles Rams
teams.headline: Rams use short bye to heal up for Green Bay

stories.text: Rams hope the bye brings Davante Adams back for Green Bay
stories.summary: The Rams are 6-4 and off this week after a 34-6 win over the Cardinals. Wide receiver Davante Adams is on injured reserve with a hamstring injury and is reportedly aiming to return against the Packers on Nov. 25. The bye lasts only 10 days because of that Wednesday game.

stories.text: Puka Nacua is on IR and not expected until mid-December
stories.summary: Nacua sprained his MCL and PCL and has turf toe, and the Rams put him on injured reserve Nov. 12. Coach Sean McVay said the timeline has not changed. He becomes eligible to return for Week 15 against the Cowboys.

stories.text: Matthew Stafford carves up Arizona on 26 throws
stories.summary: Stafford completed 18 of 26 passes for 249 yards and three touchdowns, with one interception. His 9.6 yards per attempt was the second best of his season. The scores went to Tyler Higbee, Xavier Smith and Davis Allen, a sign of how thin the receiver room has become.

stories.text: 70: Puka Nacua's catches through seven games, an NFL record
stories.summary: Nacua caught 70 passes for 715 yards and four touchdowns before the knee injury ended his run. ESPN Research says no player has had more receptions through his first seven games. Since Week 4 he led the league in both catches and receiving yards.

stories.text: Rams host the Packers Wednesday at 8 p.m. ET on Netflix
stories.summary: Los Angeles is on its bye this week, then hosts Green Bay at SoFi Stadium on Thanksgiving Eve, Nov. 25. Both teams get only 10 days between games, the shortest turnaround in the league this season. Watch how many of the injured Rams are ready on short rest.

teams.name: San Francisco 49ers
teams.headline: 49ers prep at altitude for Vikings in Mexico City

stories.text: Shanahan is 0-5 against Brian Flores defenses
stories.summary: Kyle Shanahan's offenses have never beaten a defense with Flores on the staff, and Flores now runs Minnesota's unit. The Vikings have blitzed on 72.6 percent of dropbacks. The 49ers are practicing at altitude in Colorado Springs to get ready for Mexico City.

stories.text: Evans and Greenlaw sit out; Shanahan expects both back Thursday
stories.summary: Receiver Mike Evans (Achilles) and linebacker Dre Greenlaw (neck) did not practice Wednesday. Shanahan said both could return Thursday. Cornerback Renardo Green (back) was limited and is day-to-day, and McCaffrey and Trent Williams sat for rest.

stories.text: Brock Purdy sits at 20 touchdowns and 5 interceptions
stories.summary: Purdy has thrown for 2,369 yards with 20 touchdowns and five interceptions through nine games. The 49ers are 5-0 at home and lead the NFC West at 8-1. He faces a Vikings defense that sends extra rushers more than 70 percent of the time.

stories.text: 72.6%: How often Minnesota blitzes on dropbacks
stories.summary: The Vikings have sent extra rushers on 72.6 percent of dropbacks through 10 weeks. Shanahan said facing Flores means 70 straight plays of that pressure. The 49ers will lean on quick throws and run-game answers to beat it.

stories.text: 49ers play Vikings Sunday at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC
stories.summary: San Francisco meets Minnesota (7-2) at Estadio Banorte in Mexico City on Sunday, Nov. 22. NBC and Peacock carry the game. Watch for Kyler Murray, who did not practice Wednesday with a hamstring injury.

teams.name: Seattle Seahawks
teams.headline: Seahawks eye Darnold's return after bye

stories.text: Macdonald is optimistic Darnold will play at San Francisco
stories.summary: Sam Darnold has missed two games with quadriceps and rib injuries. Coach Mike Macdonald said he is really optimistic Darnold will be available for the Nov. 29 game at the 49ers, but Darnold must handle a full week of practice first. Darnold remains the starter when healthy.

stories.text: Seahawks use bye to patch a banged-up offensive line
stories.summary: Right tackle Abraham Lucas sprained his ankle against the Raiders and did not return. Left tackle Charles Cross has missed three straight games with an ankle injury. Guard Quenton Nelson is week to week after a minor knee procedure, and Anthony Bradford is dealing with a knee issue.

stories.text: Devon Witherspoon sacks Mendoza twice on the blitz
stories.summary: Witherspoon played all 59 snaps against the Raiders and sacked Fernando Mendoza twice as a blitzer, earning a 90.4 PFF pass-rush grade. Byron Murphy II added a sack and six pressures. Seattle sacked Mendoza six times and held Las Vegas to 163 yards.

stories.text: 1,207: Jaxon Smith-Njigba's receiving yards lead the NFL
stories.summary: Smith-Njigba also leads the league with 79 catches and 10 touchdowns with seven games left. No other receiver has reached 1,000 yards. CeeDee Lamb is next at 976.

stories.text: Seahawks on bye, then at the 49ers Nov. 29 at 4:25 p.m. ET
stories.summary: Seattle is off this week at 6-4, in the hunt for the NFC's seventh seed. It visits the 8-1 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 29, with Fox carrying the game. Watch Darnold's status and the health of the offensive line.
